chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about the man who takes possession of the land with the goodwill/agreement of its owners, upon a condition he stipulated by him with them, and if he repairs in it a repair or renews in it a building, then for him is the rent/profit of its houses, except that which was in the hands of its farmers beforehand.

He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he has entered into the lease of the land upon a known matter, then he should not deal with what is in the hands of its farmers, unless he had stipulated with the owners of the land regarding what is in the hands of the farmers.'

key_terms.أَجْر: Rent, wage, or profit derived from work/improvement

ai.seo_question: What are the rights of a lessee regarding improvements and repairs made to leased land in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'iqta' or land leasing, clarifying that a lessee's right to profits from new constructions is contingent upon not infringing upon the pre-existing assets of the original landowners (dehqans) unless explicitly agreed upon. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on contractual precision and the protection of property rights within agricultural tenancy agreements. The ruling underscores the importance of clear stipulations in lease contracts to prevent disputes over improvements and existing structures.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked abou the man who leases the land with the agreement of its owners upon a stipulation he stipulates upon them, and if he were to do repairs therein from the repair work or a renewal a construction therein, so for him would be the rent of its building, except for that which was already in the hands of the former farmers beforehand.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When he had entered into a lease of the land upon a known matter, so he should not deal with what is in the hands of its farmers except he happened to have stipulated upon the owner of the land with regards to what is in the hands of the farmers’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Sama‘ah who has said the following:

“I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who formed a contract for a land without compulsion on the owners, with the condition with them that if he did certain repairs or built a building, that he would have the rent of such homes except what was in the hands of the farmers from before.

He (the Imam) said, ‘If he has entered into contract for a known matter, he must not bother with farmers unless he has set a condition with the owner to include what is in the hands of the farmers also.’”
